[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

The CI/CD pipeline template is one of five mandatory components of a Golden Path bundle, but no specification defines what stages it must contain, how it must integrate with the Verification Contract's checks, or how it must collect and submit compliance evidence. Without a specification, Platform Engineering authors each path's pipeline template ad hoc — stage composition varies between paths, Verification Contract checks are sometimes soft-blocked rather than required, compliance evidence is produced inconsistently or not at all, and credential management varies from OIDC workload identity to injected secrets. A pipeline template that does not enforce every Verification Contract check on every commit is not a conformance gate — it is a reminder. A bundle whose pipeline template does not produce compliance evidence on every build cannot substantiate its compliance claims to auditors. An ad hoc pipeline template means Infrastructure Architecture and Security Architecture review the same gaps on every ARB submission instead of reviewing a specification once.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

This pattern defines the mandatory stage composition, stage ordering constraints, three standard consumer parameters, six pipeline conformance checks (PIPE-001 through PIPE-006), the `workflow-params.yaml` manifest, compliance evidence obligations, and the verification layer integration requirements that every Golden Path CI/CD pipeline template must satisfy. A conforming template stored at `catalog/ci-cd/{path-id}/` executes all Verification Contract checks as non-optional pipeline gates, produces compliance evidence on every build run, and uses OIDC workload identity for all deployment and registry credentials — without any per-team configuration. Because the stage composition, check enforcement model, evidence collection obligations, and six pipeline conformance checks are specified here, EA Practice reviews the specification once at the catalog level. Every path that conforms to this pattern inherits that review without individual template evaluation.

[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- Authoring the CI/CD pipeline template component for a new Golden Path bundle before ARB submission
- Auditing an existing path's pipeline template for conformance prior to re-submission or compliance review
- Remediating a catalog pipeline template whose ad hoc authoring omitted required stages, used soft-blocked checks, or lacked compliance evidence collection
- Adding a language variant pipeline template to an existing path (e.g., adding a Python variant to a path that previously only had a .NET template)

### Target Audience

This pattern is intended for:

- **Platform Engineers** responsible for authoring and maintaining Golden Path CI/CD pipeline templates in the catalog
- **DevOps Engineers** managing pipeline standards, stage composition, and deployment automation
- **Solutions Architects** evaluating conformance of pipeline templates against the Verification Contract
- **Security Engineers** reviewing pipeline enforcement of SAST, dependency scanning, and PHI fitness checks
- **Site Reliability Engineers (SREs)** ensuring compliance evidence is produced systematically on every build

[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- Platform Engineering has a complete specification for what the pipeline template must contain — ad hoc authoring judgment is replaced by a checkable standard, and the pre-submission checklist in GUID-TECH-IMPL-001 verifies conformance before any ARB review is scheduled
- EA Practice reviews the specification once at the catalog level; every path whose template conforms to this pattern inherits that review without individual template re-evaluation
- Teams reference the template and receive all 17 required stages, all Verification Contract checks, full compliance evidence collection, and the production approval gate — in fewer than 15 lines of service-level pipeline configuration
- Autonomous AI agents and development teams receive a catalog entry backed by a validated pipeline template that executes the Verification Contract systematically — the constrained solution space the [Enterprise Golden Path Strategy](../../../strategy/white-papers/engineering/enterprise-golden-path-strategy.md) requires

[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

The [Enterprise Golden Path Strategy](../../../strategy/white-papers/engineering/enterprise-golden-path-strategy.md) defines the CI/CD pipeline template as one of five mandatory bundle components: *"A GitHub Actions or Azure Pipelines workflow implementing the standard build, test, security scan, and deployment stages."* Standard means the stages are the same for every service on the path — teams inherit the pipeline, they do not configure it. A pipeline that teams configure is not standard; it drifts from the moment a team makes the first local modification.

The pipeline template is the enforcement mechanism for the Verification Contract. Without a pipeline template that executes every check as a required gate, the Verification Contract is advisory: teams run the checks when they remember to, in whatever order they choose, with whatever pass/warn configuration is convenient. The compliance claims recorded in the compliance metadata file depend on the checks being executed systematically and their results being recorded as compliance evidence on every build. A Verification Contract without a pipeline template that enforces it is not a compliance program — it is documentation of intent.

Gainwell operates in a regulated environment (HIPAA, FedRAMP, ARC-AMPE). Auditors require evidence that compliance checks were executed on every build of HIPAA-scoped services. SAST results, dependency scan outputs, conformance check results, and PHI fitness function results must be traceable to specific commit SHAs and build IDs. A pipeline template that does not produce this evidence on every build, or that writes it to a non-queryable location, prevents automated compliance reporting and forces manual evidence assembly at audit time.

[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

Golden Path pipeline templates are reusable pipeline definitions stored at `catalog/ci-cd/{path-id}/` in the Golden Path Catalog repository. Service repositories reference the template using the platform's native template-reference mechanism — they do not copy or modify it.

The three supported CI/CD platforms and their template-reference mechanisms:

| Platform | Template Mechanism | Consumer Reference |
|---|---|---|
| **GitHub Actions** | `on: workflow_call` reusable workflow | `uses: org/repo/.github/workflows/ci-cd/{path-id}/workflow.yaml@vX.Y.Z` |
| **Azure Pipelines** | `extends:` YAML template in a central repository | `extends: templates/ci-cd/{path-id}/pipeline-template.yml@gpCatalog` |
| **Jenkins** | Shared Library (`@Library`) with a `call()` method | `@Library('gp-catalog@vX.Y.Z') _ + gp{PatId}Pipeline(...)` |

Pipeline template conformance is verified by six pipeline conformance checks (PIPE-001 through PIPE-006), which are evaluated against the template definition at authoring time. These checks are distinct from the Verification Contract checks (Layer 1, Layer 2, Layer 3) — the Verification Contract checks validate the *service repository*; the PIPE checks validate the *pipeline template itself*:

- **PIPE-001 — Required Stage Completeness**: All 17 required stages are present and ordered correctly. No required stage is missing or conditionally excluded on the main branch. Note: Stage 10 (Layer 3 Policy-as-Code) may be omitted for non-infrastructure paths — omission must be documented in `workflow-params.yaml` with `stage_10_policy_as_code: not_applicable` and a rationale.
- **PIPE-002 — Non-Optional Verification Steps**: Every stage that executes a Verification Contract check uses `continue-on-error: false` (GitHub Actions) / `continueOnError: false` (Azure Pipelines) / no `catchError(buildResult: 'FAILURE')` wrapper removed (Jenkins) on the main branch. Feature branches may use warn-only mode for checks added in the current path version release cycle only.
- **PIPE-003 — No Inline Credentials**: No secret value — registry password, deployment token, API key — appears inline or as a team-injectable secret for standard pipeline stages. Deployment and registry credentials use OIDC workload identity at runtime. Registry authentication uses the runner's managed identity; deployment credentials use `azure/login@v2` with `use-oidc: true` (GitHub Actions) or equivalent OIDC patterns for Azure Pipelines and Jenkins.
- **PIPE-004 — Production Approval Gate Present**: Stage 13 (Production Approval Gate) is present and configured with at least one required human approver from `platform-leads` using the platform's native environment protection mechanism. This stage is non-configurable by teams — it cannot be removed or made non-blocking.
- **PIPE-005 — Compliance Evidence Upload Present and Wired**: Stage 17 (Compliance Evidence Upload) is present, not conditional on success-only, and writes metadata fields `build_id`, `commit_sha`, `path_id`, and `path_version` to the Compliance Evidence Store on every build — including failed builds. Failed build evidence is required for incident response and audit purposes.
- **PIPE-006 — All Tool Versions Pinned**: Every tool reference — `uses:` actions, scanner tools, CLI versions — specifies an exact version (SHA or semver tag). No `@latest`, `@main`, or floating version reference in any required stage. Tool version changes go through the standard path update process.

The four verification layers are integrated at specific pipeline stages:

| Verification Layer | Pipeline Stage | Gate Type |
|---|---|---|
| **Layer 1 — Conformance Gate** | Stage 2 | Blocks all subsequent stages; runs on every trigger |
| **Layer 2 — Fitness Functions** | Stage 9 | Blocks promotion to staging; runs on push to main |
| **Layer 2 — PHI Fitness Functions** | Stage 16 | Blocks evidence upload for HIPAA paths; runs on push to main |
| **Layer 3 — Policy-as-Code** | Stage 10 | Blocks `terraform apply`; runs on push to main for infra paths |
| **Layer 4 — Runtime Monitors** | Stage 15 | Provisions monitors on first production deployment |

[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

Without a pipeline template specification:

- **Verification Contract checks become advisory rather than mandatory**: Without a specification requiring that every Verification Contract check is non-optional on the main branch, authors commonly add checks with `continue-on-error: true` to allow the pipeline to pass while surfacing failure information. A check configured with `continue-on-error: true` is not a gate — it is a log entry. The compliance evidence produced by a soft-blocked check is not evidence of a passing gate; it is evidence that the check ran. An auditor reviewing compliance evidence for a HIPAA path expects every check to be a hard gate; a soft-blocked check produces passing evidence for a failing assertion. This is the highest-risk configuration error possible in a compliance pipeline — it makes non-compliance invisible.

- **Compliance evidence is either absent or non-queryable**: Without a required Stage 17 specification, compliance evidence collection is left to individual template authors. Common outcomes: scan outputs are written as pipeline artifacts but not uploaded to the Compliance Evidence Store; evidence files are written with inconsistent metadata fields (missing `commit_sha`, absent `path_id`); evidence is only collected on successful builds, meaning failed builds — which include the most compliance-relevant events — have no evidence record. Automated compliance reporting (PTN-GOV-AI-004) depends on evidence being queryable by `path_id`, `commit_sha`, and `build_id`. Evidence without these fields cannot be aggregated for compliance reporting and must be retrieved manually per audit request.

- **Inline credentials create a persistent security exposure**: Without a specification prohibiting team-injectable credentials, pipeline authors frequently use `secrets.REGISTRY_PASSWORD` or `secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN` as inputs that teams configure in their service repositories. A credential configured by a team is a credential configured with the team's access scope — not the path's least-privilege access scope. Credential rotation is uncoordinated across teams. A credential stored in a GitHub Actions secret is accessible to any workflow in the repository. OIDC workload identity eliminates the credential surface entirely — there is no secret to inject, rotate, or leak.

- **Production deployments proceed without human sign-off**: Without a required production approval gate, pipeline authors may wire `deploy-production` as a direct successor to `deploy-staging`. In a regulated environment, all production deployments to HIPAA-scoped services require a human approval step documented in the compliance evidence. A production deployment without an approval record is a compliance gap that surfaces at the next HIPAA audit. The approval gate is not configurable; it is structural.

[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

- The Verification Contract's Layer 1 and Layer 2 check commands must be finalized before the pipeline template is authored — the pipeline executes commands defined in the contract; if the commands change after the template is authored, the template must be updated to match
- The scaffold template and the pipeline template are authored concurrently — the scaffold's unit tests must pass when executed by the pipeline during template validation; scaffolds and pipelines that are authored in isolation frequently have incompatible test invocation patterns
- Pipeline template version is part of path version — a path version `v1.3.0` has a pipeline template `v1.3.0`; the pipeline template cannot be updated independently without a path version change
- All scan outputs, check results, and fitness function results must be written to `reports/` in the build workspace before the compliance evidence upload step runs — the Compliance Evidence Store step collects everything from that directory; scan tools that write to arbitrary locations require a `cp` step to collect before evidence upload
- Scanner thresholds (CVSS score for SCA, severity for Trivy) are path constants in the template — they are not team-configurable inputs. HIPAA and FedRAMP paths must use `CVSS ≥ 7.0` for SCA and `CRITICAL|HIGH` for Trivy on production branches. Configurable thresholds mean teams can disable the scan by setting the threshold to `10.0`

[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

A conforming Golden Path CI/CD pipeline template is a reusable workflow definition stored at `catalog/ci-cd/{path-id}/` that, when referenced by a service repository, executes all 17 required stages in the correct order, enforces every Verification Contract check as a non-optional gate on the main branch, uses OIDC workload identity for all deployment and registry credentials, produces compliance evidence on every build, and requires human approval before every production deployment. The template satisfies this pattern when it passes PIPE-001 through PIPE-006 during pre-submission validation, a `workflow-params.yaml` manifest is present at the template root, and an end-to-end dry-run against a scaffold-instantiated test service completes with all stages passing and compliance evidence confirmed in the Compliance Evidence Store.

The 17 required stages define the structural minimum every conforming template must implement regardless of CI/CD platform:

| Stage | Trigger | HIPAA-Only | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1. Compile / Build** | all | | Compile the project; fail immediately on compile error |
| **2. Layer 1 — Conformance Gate** | all | | Run `conformance-check`; all Layer 1 checks from the Verification Contract must pass |
| **3. Unit Tests** | all | | Run the service's unit test suite; 100% pass rate required on main |
| **4. SAST Scan** | all | | Run static analysis (CodeQL or equivalent); upload SARIF to security findings store and to `reports/` |
| **5. SCA — Dependency Vulnerability Scan** | all | | Run dependency scan (OWASP Dependency-Check or Snyk); fail on CVSS ≥ 7.0 on production branches |
| **6. Build Artifact** | push | | Build and package the path's deployable artifact; artifact is tagged with commit SHA and path version; artifact type, build tool, and base image or base package are path constants — not team inputs (e.g., container image via `docker build`; npm bundle via `npm run build`; Python wheel via `python -m build`; NuGet package via `dotnet pack`) |
| **7. Artifact Security Scan** | push | | Run a security scan appropriate to the artifact type; fail on path-constant severity threshold; output written to `reports/artifact-scan.json` (e.g., Trivy for container images; Snyk or `npm audit` for npm bundles; `safety` or Snyk for Python wheels) |
| **8. Publish to Approved Artifact Store** | push to main | | Publish the artifact to the approved artifact management endpoint for the path's workload class using OIDC workload identity; do not publish to public artifact stores; endpoint is a path constant declared in `workflow-params.yaml` |
| **9. Layer 2 — Fitness Functions** | push to main | | Deploy to CI test environment; run `fitness-function-runner`; all Layer 2 checks must pass |
| **10. Layer 3 — Policy-as-Code** | push to main | | Run `opa eval` against Terraform plan; all Layer 3 checks must pass before `terraform apply`; omit for non-infrastructure paths with documented rationale |
| **11. Deploy to Staging** | push to main | | Deploy to staging using workload identity; no manual credential injection |
| **12. Staging Smoke Test** | push to main | | Call `GET /health` and `GET /info` on deployed staging instance; both must return HTTP 200 |
| **13. Production Approval Gate** | push to main | | Mandatory human approval; minimum 1 approval from `platform-leads`; non-configurable |
| **14. Deploy to Production** | after approval | | Deploy to production using workload identity |
| **15. Layer 4 — Monitor Provisioning** | first prod deploy | | Run `invariant-monitor-provisioner`; activates runtime monitors for this deployment |
| **16. PHI Fitness Functions** | push to main | ✅ | Deploy synthetic PHI-bearing requests; PHI string must not appear in log output (FF-001) |
| **17. Compliance Evidence Upload** | always | | Upload all scan outputs and check results to Compliance Evidence Store with `build_id`, `commit_sha`, `path_id`, `path_version` |

[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#architecture-diagram]

### Architecture Diagram

```
catalog/ci-cd/{path-id}/
├── workflow-params.yaml     ← Declares required stages, check IDs wired at each stage, compliance scope
│                              PIPE check IDs, and platform (github-actions / azure-pipelines / jenkins)
└── workflow.yaml            ← Reusable pipeline definition (on: workflow_call / extends: / @Library)
   OR pipeline-template.yml     Three consumer inputs: service_name, team, environment
   OR vars/gp{N}Pipeline.groovy  All other configuration is path constants

    Four-Layer Verification Architecture Integration
    ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  Layer 1 — Conformance Gate                          Pipeline Stage 2         │
    │    PTN-INFRA-GOV-001 defines the conformance-check tool                       │
    │    Executes all Layer 1 checks from the Verification Contract (PTN-GOV-AI-003)│
    │    Runs on every trigger (PR and push); non-optional; blocks all later stages │
    │    Checks: structural presence, metadata fields, dependency declarations,      │
    │            Golden Path identifier declared in scaffold, manifest completeness  │
    ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    │  Layer 2 — Fitness Functions                         Pipeline Stage 9, 16     │
    │    PTN-APP-GOV-001 defines the fitness-function-runner tool                   │
    │    Executes all Layer 2 checks from the Verification Contract (PTN-GOV-AI-003)│
    │    Stage 9: behavioral checks (health endpoint, API contract, etc.)            │
    │    Stage 16: PHI checks — PHI in logs assertion (HIPAA paths only)            │
    │    Runs on push to main; blocks promotion to staging on failure               │
    ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    │  Layer 3 — Policy-as-Code                            Pipeline Stage 10        │
    │    PTN-INFRA-GOV-002 defines the OPA/Rego policy evaluation tool             │
    │    Executes all Layer 3 checks from the Verification Contract (PTN-GOV-AI-003)│
    │    Runs opa eval against terraform show -json plan output                     │
    │    Blocks terraform apply on any check failure                                │
    │    Infrastructure paths only; omit with documented rationale for other paths  │
    ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    │  Layer 4 — Runtime Monitors                          Pipeline Stage 15        │
    │    PTN-APP-GOV-003 defines the runtime behavioral invariant monitor           │
    │    Provisions drift detection monitors via invariant-monitor-provisioner      │
    │    Runs on first production deployment only; monitors run continuously        │
    │    Depends on path-tagged resources (Layer 4 requires attribution tags)       │
    └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    Consumer parameters (three; all others are path constants in the template)
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  service_name   → identity names, namespace, image tag, deployment target refs │
    │  team           → team attribution in compliance evidence metadata             │
    │  environment    → target environment for staging deploy; default: staging      │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    Compliance Evidence Obligations (Stage 17 — always runs, including on failure)
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  conformance-layer1.json       → Layer 1 check results (all runs)              │
    │  sast-results.sarif            → Static analysis output (all runs)             │
    │  dependency-scan.json          → SCA output (all runs)                         │
    │  trivy-image-scan.json         → Container image scan output (push runs)       │
    │  fitness-functions.json        → Layer 2 check results (main branch runs)      │
    │  phi-fitness.json              → PHI check results (HIPAA paths, main branch)  │
    │  opa-evidence-{id}.json        → Layer 3 check results (infra paths)           │
    │  Metadata required on every record: build_id, commit_sha, path_id, path_version│
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component | Responsibility | Conformance Check |
|---|---|---|
| `workflow-params.yaml` | Machine-readable manifest declaring the path ID, CI/CD platform, wired check IDs at each stage, compliance scope, and any stage omissions with documented rationale. Consumed by the ARB review process to verify conformance against this pattern. | PIPE-001 (stage presence confirmed by comparing declared stages against this specification) |
| **Stage 2 — Layer 1 Conformance Gate** | Executes `conformance-check` using Layer 1 check IDs from the Verification Contract. Non-optional; runs before unit tests on every trigger. Blocks all subsequent stages on failure. | PIPE-002 (non-optional assertion) |
| **Stage 4 — SAST Scan** | Runs static analysis (CodeQL or equivalent) with pinned version. Uploads SARIF output to both the platform's security findings store and `reports/` for evidence collection. Fail threshold is a path constant — not a team input. | PIPE-006 (version pinned), PIPE-005 (output written to `reports/`) |
| **Stage 5 — SCA Scan** | Runs dependency vulnerability scan with pinned version. Fail threshold (CVSS ≥ 7.0 on production branches) is a path constant. | PIPE-006 (version pinned) |
| **Stage 7 — Container Image Scan** | Runs Trivy against the built image. Fail severity (`CRITICAL\|HIGH`) is a path constant. Required for all HIPAA and FedRAMP paths. | PIPE-006 (version pinned) |
| **Stage 9 — Layer 2 Fitness Functions** | Runs `fitness-function-runner` with Layer 2 check IDs from the Verification Contract against a deployed CI test instance. Non-optional on main. Blocks staging deploy on failure. | PIPE-002 (non-optional assertion) |
| **Stage 10 — Layer 3 Policy-as-Code** | Runs `opa eval` against the infrastructure module's `terraform show -json` plan output. Non-optional for infrastructure paths. Blocks `terraform apply` on failure. Omittable for non-infrastructure paths with a `workflow-params.yaml` rationale entry. | PIPE-002 (non-optional assertion), PIPE-001 (omission documented) |
| **Stage 13 — Production Approval Gate** | Requires minimum 1 human approval from `platform-leads` using the platform's environment protection mechanism. Non-configurable by teams. Blocks production deploy until approval is recorded. | PIPE-004 (approval gate present and configured) |
| **Stage 15 — Layer 4 Monitor Provisioning** | Runs `invariant-monitor-provisioner` on first production deployment to activate runtime drift detection and behavioral invariant monitors. | PIPE-001 (stage presence) |
| **Stage 16 — PHI Fitness Functions** | HIPAA paths only. Runs PHI-bearing synthetic requests against the deployed staging instance; asserts PHI string does not appear in log output. Non-optional for HIPAA-scoped paths on main. | PIPE-002 (non-optional for HIPAA), PIPE-001 (present for HIPAA scope) |
| **Stage 17 — Compliance Evidence Upload** | Runs `evidence-uploader` to write all `reports/` artifacts to the Compliance Evidence Store. Configured as `if: always()` — runs on success and failure. Records `build_id`, `commit_sha`, `path_id`, `path_version` metadata on every record. | PIPE-005 (evidence upload present and always-run) |
| **OIDC Workload Identity** | All deployment steps (Stages 11, 14) and registry push (Stage 8) authenticate using OIDC workload identity — `azure/login@v2` with `use-oidc: true` (GitHub Actions), Azure Pipelines service connection with workload identity federation, or Jenkins OIDC credential binding. No inline secrets or team-injectable credentials for standard pipeline stages. | PIPE-003 (no inline credentials) |

[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

1. The Verification Contract author finalizes Layer 1 and Layer 2 check IDs before pipeline template authoring begins (GUID-GOV-IMPL-001 Phases 1–3). Layer 1 check IDs are wired at Stage 2; Layer 2 check IDs are wired at Stage 9. If Layer 3 check IDs are also finalized (GUID-INFRA-IMPL-001 Phase 7 complete), they are wired at Stage 10 for infrastructure paths.
2. The scaffold author and the pipeline template author work concurrently — the scaffold's unit test invocation pattern must be compatible with Stage 3's test runner invocation. Both authors must confirm the test invocation command before Stage 3 is wired.
3. The infrastructure module's `isolation-baseline-{path-id}-{version}.txt` and `identity-chain-{path-id}-{version}.txt` evidence files (from GUID-INFRA-IMPL-001 Phase 6) are referenced in the compliance metadata (GUID-GOV-IMPL-002) — the pipeline template's Stage 17 is responsible for ensuring that equivalent evidence produced at service build time is also uploaded with the correct metadata format.
4. At each pipeline execution, Stage 2 calls `conformance-check --path-id {path-id}` which loads the path's Verification Contract from `catalog/verification/{path-id}/` and evaluates every Layer 1 check against the calling service repository. No check ID is hardcoded in the pipeline template — all check IDs are loaded from the contract, which means updating the contract's check list automatically updates what the pipeline enforces without requiring a pipeline template change.
5. The `invariant-monitor-provisioner` (Stage 15) reads the Verification Contract to determine which runtime monitor rules to activate. It requires the infrastructure module's `path_id` tag on all provisioned resources to attribute drift events to the correct path. Stage 15 executes only on the first production deployment; subsequent deployments skip it via the platform's environment deployment history.
6. Service repositories pin to a specific path version tag using the platform's version reference mechanism (`@vX.Y.Z` for GitHub Actions, `ref: refs/tags/vX.Y.Z` for Azure Pipelines, `@Library('gp-catalog@vX.Y.Z')` for Jenkins). When the path publishes a new version, team adoption is voluntary until the adoption deadline set in the adoption playbook (GUID-GOV-PROC-003).

[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

**HIPAA-scoped paths**: Stage 16 (PHI Fitness Functions) is mandatory. The PHI fitness function asserts that strings matching the PHI pattern regex (defined in the Verification Contract as FF-PHI-001) do not appear in service log output after a synthetic PHI-bearing request. Stage 5 (SCA) fail threshold must be `CVSS ≥ 7.0`. Stage 7 (Trivy) fail severity must be `CRITICAL|HIGH`.

**FedRAMP Moderate paths**: Stage 10 (Layer 3 Policy-as-Code) is mandatory and includes FedRAMP-specific OPA checks (secrets store deletion protection, TLS 1.3 minimum) in addition to the base TF check set. Stage 17 evidence must be retained for a minimum of 3 years (aligned with FedRAMP continuous monitoring requirements).

**ARC-AMPE paths (CMS Medicaid)**: Co-applicable with HIPAA. All HIPAA requirements apply. Stage 2 (Conformance Gate) includes the ARC-AMPE tag assertion check (`TF-ARC-001`). Stage 17 evidence metadata must include `arc_ampe_scope: "true"`.

**Non-infrastructure paths (MFE/CDN, Batch, API-only)**: Stage 10 (Layer 3 Policy-as-Code) is omitted. Omission must be documented in `workflow-params.yaml` as `stage_10_policy_as_code: not_applicable` with a rationale string. Stage 15 (Layer 4 Monitor Provisioning) uses the path's technology-profile-appropriate monitor configuration rather than the Kubernetes-focused default.

**Multi-language variant paths**: A path that supports both .NET and Python workloads may have two pipeline template files at `catalog/ci-cd/{path-id}/workflow-dotnet.yaml` and `catalog/ci-cd/{path-id}/workflow-python.yaml`. Both must satisfy PIPE-001 through PIPE-006. The `workflow-params.yaml` manifest must declare all language variants. A `compile_command` and `test_command` path constant differs between variants; all security and compliance stages are identical.

### Prerequisites

- Verification Contract Layer 1 and Layer 2 check IDs finalized (GUID-GOV-IMPL-001 Phases 1–3) — check IDs are wired at Stages 2 and 9; the pipeline cannot be validated without them
- Scaffold template authored and repo structure confirmed (GUID-APP-IMPL-003) — Stage 3 unit test invocation must match the scaffold's test runner pattern
- Approved artifact management endpoint confirmed with Platform Infrastructure for the target path — endpoint type is workload-class-specific and must be declared as `artifact_store` in `workflow-params.yaml` before Phase 3 begins; see GUID-GOV-PROC-004 §Technical Prerequisites for the workload-class-to-endpoint mapping (container registry, npm registry, PyPI-compatible feed, NuGet feed, or blob storage)
- OIDC workload identity configured for CI/CD runner in staging and production environments — `azure/login@v2` OIDC federation (GitHub Actions), Azure Pipelines service connection with workload identity federation, or Jenkins OIDC credential binding plugin

[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#phase-1-template-root-and-manifest]

#### Phase 1: Template Root and Manifest

1. Create `catalog/ci-cd/{path-id}/workflow-params.yaml` declaring the path ID, CI/CD platform, compliance scope, all 17 stage slots with the Verification Contract check IDs wired at each applicable stage, and any stage omissions with rationale. This is the ARB reviewer's machine-readable record for the pipeline component.
2. Create the platform-specific template file:
   - GitHub Actions: `workflow.yaml` with `on: workflow_call`
   - Azure Pipelines: `pipeline-template.yml` with `parameters:` and `stages:`
   - Jenkins: `vars/gp{N}Pipeline.groovy` with `def call(Map params)`
3. Define the three consumer inputs: `service_name`, `team`, `environment`. Add a boolean `dry_run` input (default: `false`) that skips all deployment stages but runs all verification stages. All other configuration is a path constant.
4. Add all 17 stage slots as empty jobs/stages with correct sequential dependencies. Validate the template is syntactically valid before wiring any stage content.

[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#phase-2-build-and-static-analysis-stages-stages-15]

#### Phase 2: Build and Static Analysis Stages (Stages 1–5)

5. Wire Stage 1 (Compile) with the language-appropriate build command for the path's stack. Language runtime version is a path constant.
6. Wire Stage 2 (Conformance Gate) loading Layer 1 check IDs from the Verification Contract: `conformance-check --path-id {path-id} --contract catalog/verification/{path-id}/verification-contract.yaml --checks layer1 --output reports/conformance-layer1.json`.
7. Wire Stage 3 (Unit Tests) with the scaffold's test runner invocation pattern. 100% pass rate required on main.
8. Wire Stage 4 (SAST) with pinned CodeQL version. Output written to `reports/sast-results.sarif`. Upload SARIF to the platform's security findings store.
9. Wire Stage 5 (SCA) with pinned OWASP Dependency-Check or Snyk version. CVSS fail threshold is a path constant (minimum `7.0` for HIPAA/FedRAMP). Output written to `reports/dependency-scan.json`.
10. Run Stages 1–5 against the scaffold in dry-run mode. All must pass before wiring image stages.

#### Phase 3: Artifact Build, Scan, and Publish Stages (Stages 6–8)

11. Wire Stage 6 (Build Artifact) using the build tool and artifact type declared in `workflow-params.yaml` for the path's workload class. Artifact tag/version format: `{service_name}:{commit-sha}-{path-version}`. The build tool, base image or base package, and runtime version are path constants — not team inputs. (e.g., container image paths: `docker build --build-arg BASE_IMAGE={artifact_store}/base:{version}`; npm bundle paths: `npm run build` with pinned Node version; Python wheel paths: `python -m build` with pinned Python version)
12. Wire Stage 7 (Artifact Security Scan) with a pinned tool version appropriate to the artifact type. Fail severity threshold is a path constant. Output written to `reports/artifact-scan.json`. (e.g., Trivy `0.58.2` for container images with `CRITICAL|HIGH`; Snyk or `npm audit` for npm bundles; `safety` for Python wheels)
13. Wire Stage 8 (Publish to Approved Artifact Store) using OIDC workload identity authentication. The `artifact_store` endpoint is a path constant from `workflow-params.yaml`. Do not add artifact management credentials as team-injectable inputs.

#### Phase 4: Deployment and Verification Stages (Stages 9–15)

14. Wire Stage 9 (Fitness Functions) loading Layer 2 check IDs from the Verification Contract: `fitness-function-runner --path-id {path-id} --contract catalog/verification/{path-id}/verification-contract.yaml --checks layer2 --target https://{service_name}.ci.internal --output reports/fitness-functions.json`.

Wire Stage 13 (Production Approval Gate) using the platform's environment protection mechanism: GitHub environment protection rule with minimum 1 approver from `platform-leads`; Azure Pipelines deployment environment with required approval check; Jenkins `input` step with `submitter: platform-leads`. This stage is non-configurable.
18. Wire Stage 14 (Deploy to Production) using OIDC authentication.
19. Wire Stage 15 (Monitor Provisioning): `invariant-monitor-provisioner --contract catalog/verification/{path-id}/verification-contract.yaml --service {service_name}`. Configure to run on first production deploy only via environment deployment history condition.

  - stage: 2

  - stage: 3

  - stage: 4

  - stage: 11

[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

- **Author the Verification Contract before the pipeline.** The pipeline template wires check IDs from the Verification Contract at Stages 2 and 9. If the contract is not finalized, the pipeline references check commands that may change. Authoring the pipeline first means rework when the contract changes. Author GUID-GOV-IMPL-001 Phases 1–3 first; then author the pipeline.
- **Run the full pipeline against a scaffold-instantiated test service, not a synthetic fixture.** A test run against a minimal fixture confirms syntax but not integration. A test run against a real scaffold-instantiated service confirms that Stage 3's unit test invocation matches the scaffold's test runner, Stage 2's conformance check passes on real scaffold output, and Stage 9's fitness function runner can reach and measure the deployed service.
- **Wire Stage 17 as `if: always()` — including on failure.** Failed build compliance evidence is more important for audit purposes than success evidence — it proves the gate worked. A Stage 17 that only runs on success means a pipeline that fails at Stage 4 (SAST finding) produces no evidence that the SAST check ran and blocked the build. That is precisely the evidence an auditor needs for a HIPAA-regulated path.
- **Document every stage omission in `workflow-params.yaml`.** Absence of Stage 10 in a template that does not have a `stage_10_policy_as_code: not_applicable` entry in its manifest will fail PIPE-001 during pre-submission validation. An accepted absence is explicit; a gap discovered at ARB is not.
- **Pin all tool versions to a specific SHA or semver tag — not a floating tag.** A scanner pinned to `@latest` can silently adopt a new version between two pipeline runs that produces different results for the same commit. Reproducible compliance evidence requires reproducible tooling.
page_texts.33:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

- **Soft-blocking a Verification Contract check on main.** Adding `continue-on-error: true` to Stage 2 or Stage 9 to keep builds green while a check failure is being investigated transforms the check from a gate into a notification — PIPE-002 will catch this at pre-submission validation. Use `if: github.ref != 'refs/heads/main'` to enable warn-only mode on feature branches; on main the check must be hard.
- **Making scanner thresholds team-injectable inputs.** Exposing `sast_fail_threshold`, `cvss_threshold`, or `trivy_severity` as `inputs:` to the template means teams can set them to non-blocking values. These are path constants — not consumer inputs.
- **Omitting Stage 17 on failure paths.** The platform syntax for unconditional job execution differs by platform and is easy to omit: `if: always()` (GitHub Actions), `condition: always()` (Azure Pipelines), `post { always { ... } }` (Jenkins). Without it, Stage 17 does not run when earlier stages fail — exactly the scenario where compliance evidence of a check failure is needed.
- **Using a single environment for both staging and production without an approval gate.** Azure Pipelines and Jenkins allow deployment to production environments without an approval check unless the environment is explicitly configured with a required approval policy. GitHub Actions environments require explicit configuration of environment protection rules. PIPE-004 checks for the presence of the approval gate in the template definition but cannot verify the platform's environment configuration — confirm the environment protection rule exists before the ARB dry-run.
- **Adding team-injectable secret inputs for deployment credentials.** A `secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN` input that teams configure means teams control what identity the pipeline uses for production deployments. OIDC workload identity is non-injectable by design — the runner's identity is configured at the platform level, not per-service-repository.

[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#standards-alignment]

### Standards Alignment

The pipeline template is the execution layer for the Verification Contract (PTN-GOV-AI-003). Every Layer 1, Layer 2, and Layer 3 check declared in the contract must execute as a non-optional gate in the pipeline template. The PIPE-001 through PIPE-006 checks assert that the template satisfies the structural requirements of this pattern.

For regulated paths, the pipeline generates compliance evidence required to substantiate the following controls:

| NIST 800-53 r5 Control | Control Name | Pipeline Stage | Evidence Produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| SI-3 | Malicious Code Protection | Stage 7 (Trivy image scan) | `trivy-image-scan.json` |
| SI-7 | Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity | Stage 6 (image digest pinning) | Image digest in build log |
| RA-5 | Vulnerability Scanning | Stage 5 (SCA dependency scan) | `dependency-scan.json` |
| SA-11 | Developer Testing and Evaluation | Stage 4 (SAST), Stage 3 (unit tests) | `sast-results.sarif`, test results |
| AU-2 | Event Logging | Stage 17 (compliance evidence upload) | Evidence Store records per build |
| AU-9 | Protection of Audit Information | Stage 17 (evidence upload with metadata) | Immutable records in Compliance Evidence Store |
| CM-2 | Baseline Configuration | Stage 2 (Conformance Gate) | `conformance-layer1.json` |
| CM-3 | Configuration Change Control | Stage 13 (Production Approval Gate) | Approval record in platform event log |
| CA-2 | Control Assessments | Stages 4, 5, 9, 10 (all verification layers) | Aggregated evidence per build in Compliance Evidence Store |

page_texts.37:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#compliance-requirements]

### Compliance Requirements

The pipeline template is submitted as part of the complete Golden Path bundle ARB submission. The ARB will not approve a bundle without a pipeline template that:
1. Passes all six PIPE conformance checks (PIPE-001 through PIPE-006)
2. Completes a full end-to-end test run against a scaffold-instantiated test service with all stages passing
3. Produces a queryable compliance evidence record in the Compliance Evidence Store from the test run

Minor pipeline updates (tool version bumps, adding a new optional stage for a language variant) may follow the minor update process (PTN-GOV-AI-001). Changes to required stage composition, check IDs, fail thresholds, or environment progression model require ARB review. Changes that affect any security-bearing configuration (credential model, approval gate, check enforcement mode) require EA Practice sign-off regardless of version increment magnitude.
page_texts.38:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#approval-process]

### Approval Process

- **New pipeline template (first publication)**: Platform Engineering review → EA Practice review → ARB approval as part of complete Golden Path bundle
- **Verification check enforcement mode change (warn-only → hard fail)**: EA Practice review required; this is a breaking change for teams currently relying on the warn-only behavior
- **New required stage addition (applies to all adopters of this path version)**: ARB review required; triggers a major version increment
- **Tool version bump (scanner, action version)**: Minor update process (PTN-GOV-AI-001); no ARB required if the version change is pin-only with no behavior change
- **Emergency security patch (CVE in scanner tool version)**: Express review; EA Practice sign-off in lieu of full ARB; 48-hour SLA

[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#monitoring-and-metrics]

### Monitoring and Metrics

| Metric | Verification Layer | Target | Measurement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workflow-params.yaml` present at `catalog/ci-cd/{path-id}/` | Layer 1 | 100% | Catalog conformance check result |
| PIPE-001 through PIPE-006 all pass on current template definition | Pattern | 100% | Pre-submission validation run results |
| Stage 2 (Conformance Gate) hard-fail rate on main — checks blocked builds that should be blocked | Layer 1 | Track trend | CI/CD pipeline event log |
| Stage 9 (Fitness Function) pass rate on main | Layer 2 | 100% (after initial path stabilization) | Compliance Evidence Store query by `path_id` + stage |
| Compliance evidence record present in evidence store per build | All | 100% | Compliance Evidence Store completeness check |
| Stage 17 evidence records queryable by `commit_sha` | All | 100% | Evidence store query validation |
| Production deployments without Stage 13 approval record | — | 0 | Platform deployment event log query |
| Builds with inline credential use (any `secrets.*` used in deployment stages) | — | 0 | Pipeline definition PIPE-003 scan result |

[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#real-world-example-1-first-arb-submission--gp-001-pipeline-template]

### Real-World Example 1: First ARB Submission — GP-001 Pipeline Template

**Context:** Platform Engineering is authoring the complete GP-001 bundle. The pipeline template is authored after the Verification Contract (GUID-GOV-IMPL-001) and concurrently with the scaffold (GUID-APP-IMPL-003), because Stage 3 requires the scaffold's unit test invocation pattern and Stage 2 requires the Layer 1 check IDs.

**Implementation:** The pipeline template author obtains the finalized Layer 1 check IDs (SC-001 through SC-006) and Layer 2 check IDs (FF-001 through FF-004) from the Verification Contract. The scaffold author confirms the unit test invocation command (`dotnet test`). Stage 2 is wired using the Layer 1 check IDs; Stage 9 is wired using the Layer 2 check IDs. All tools are pinned to exact versions. Stage 13 uses a GitHub environment protection rule requiring 1 approval from `platform-leads`. Stage 17 is configured as `if: always()`. Stage 16 (PHI fitness functions) is present because GP-001 is HIPAA-scoped. `workflow-params.yaml` is authored concurrently. PIPE-001 through PIPE-006 all pass. A full pipeline test run against a scaffold-instantiated GP-001 test service completes with all 17 stages passing and a compliance evidence record confirmed in the Compliance Evidence Store.

**Outcome:** Bundle submitted to ARB in one cycle — no rework for pipeline defects.

[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#real-world-example-2-new-compliance-requirement-propagates-to-all-adopters]

### Real-World Example 2: New Compliance Requirement Propagates to All Adopters

**Context:** A regulatory change requires all GP-001 services to enforce TLS 1.3 minimum on all ingress connections. Platform Engineering updates the Verification Contract (new Layer 3 check `OPA-003`) and must update the pipeline template to wire the new check at Stage 10.

**Implementation:** `workflow-params.yaml` Stage 10 `check_ids` entry is updated to add `OPA-003`. Stage 10 in the pipeline template picks up the new check from the Verification Contract — no stage content changes are required because Stage 10 calls `opa eval` using the contract's full Layer 3 check set rather than individually hardcoded check commands. GP-001 is published as `v1.3.0`. Service repositories pinned to `@v1.3.0` automatically run `OPA-003` on their next commit.

**Outcome:** 100% of GP-001 adopters enforce TLS 1.3 on their next pipeline run after upgrading to `v1.3.0` — no per-team pipeline change required.

[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#scenario-1-non-infrastructure-path--stage-10-omission]

#### Scenario 1: Non-Infrastructure Path — Stage 10 Omission

Platform Engineering is authoring the GP-010 MFE/CDN path. GP-010 has no Terraform infrastructure module; the CDN distribution is a platform-managed resource, not a path-managed resource. Stage 10 (Layer 3 Policy-as-Code) is not applicable. The `workflow-params.yaml` entry for Stage 10 reads:
```yaml
  - stage: 10
    name: policy_as_code
    stage_10_policy_as_code: not_applicable
    rationale: "GP-010 deploys MFE static assets to a CDN; there is no Terraform
                plan to evaluate. CDN configuration is managed by the platform
                infrastructure team via PTN-INFRA-GOV-003."
```
PIPE-001 checks for this entry and accepts the absence of Stage 10 in the template. The ARB reviewer sees the explicit omission in `workflow-params.yaml` rather than discovering an unexplained gap.

[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#scenario-2-soft-blocked-check-discovered-at-pre-submission-validation]

#### Scenario 2: Soft-Blocked Check Discovered at Pre-Submission Validation

During Phase 6 (validation), the PIPE-002 check fails: Stage 9 has `continue-on-error: true` because the fitness function runner was producing intermittent CI environment failures during authoring. PIPE-002 requires that no Stage 9 step use `continue-on-error: true` on the main branch trigger. Resolution: the CI environment instability is investigated (found to be a DNS resolution timeout in the CI test cluster); the root cause is fixed; `continue-on-error: true` is removed. PIPE-002 now passes. Stage 9 is confirmed as a hard gate on main. Validation moves to the end-to-end test run.

[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#before-problem-state]

#### Before (Problem State)

Without a pipeline template specification, Platform Engineering authors each path's CI/CD pipeline template against convention. Some templates include all compliance-relevant stages; others omit SAST, run dependency scans with no fail threshold, or soft-block the conformance gate. Deployment credentials are injected as team-injectable secrets on some paths. Stage 17 is present on some templates but only runs on success. The compliance metadata references evidence file paths that the pipeline template does not produce. ARB reviewers cannot confirm from the template definition alone which Verification Contract checks are enforced, which are advisory, and which are missing. Auditors assembling compliance evidence for a HIPAA-scoped path must manually correlate commit SHAs to individual build artifacts because the evidence store records lack the `commit_sha` and `path_id` fields the query requires.

A team consuming a path with an ad hoc pipeline references fewer than 15 lines but inherits an unknown check enforcement profile — they cannot verify from the service repository which checks are gates and which are notifications without reading the full pipeline template definition. When a security finding surfaces in production, the incident response team cannot confirm from the audit trail whether the relevant check ran and failed (meaning someone soft-blocked it) or genuinely was not present.
page_texts.48:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#after-solution-state]

#### After (Solution State)

With a conforming pipeline template, every service on every path enforces every Verification Contract check as a non-optional gate — on every commit to main. Every build produces a compliance evidence record in the Compliance Evidence Store queryable by `path_id`, `commit_sha`, and `build_id`. Production deployments for every HIPAA-scoped service on every path have an approval record in the platform's deployment event log. When a security finding surfaces, the incident response team finds the SAST result, the Trivy image scan, and the conformance gate result for the exact commit SHA in the evidence store within seconds. Teams write fewer than 15 lines of service-level pipeline configuration; the rest is governed by the catalog.

[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem:** The CI/CD pipeline template is one of five mandatory Golden Path bundle components, but no specification defines what stages it must contain, how it must integrate with the Verification Contract's checks, or how it must produce compliance evidence. Platform Engineering authors each template ad hoc — Verification Contract checks are soft-blocked on some paths, compliance evidence is absent or unqueryable, deployment credentials are team-injectable secrets rather than OIDC workload identity, and production approval gates are missing or optional. A soft-blocked check is not a compliance gate; it is a notification. Without a pipeline template specification, the Verification Contract is documentation of intent rather than an enforcement program.

**Solution:** This pattern defines the 17 required pipeline stages, their ordering constraints, the three standard consumer inputs, six pipeline conformance checks (PIPE-001 through PIPE-006), the `workflow-params.yaml` manifest, and the verification layer integration requirements every Golden Path CI/CD pipeline template must satisfy. A conforming template executes all Verification Contract checks as non-optional gates, produces queryable compliance evidence on every build including failure, uses OIDC workload identity for all deployment and registry credentials, and requires human approval before every production deployment — without any team configuration.

**When to Use:**
- Authoring the CI/CD pipeline template component for a new Golden Path bundle before ARB submission
- Auditing an existing path's pipeline template for conformance prior to re-submission or compliance review
- Remediating a catalog pipeline template whose ad hoc authoring used soft-blocked checks, lacked compliance evidence collection, or used team-injectable deployment credentials

**Key Benefits:**
- Teams reference the template in fewer than 15 lines and inherit all 17 stages, all Verification Contract checks as hard gates, full compliance evidence collection, and the production approval gate — with no per-stage configuration
- Every build produces a compliance evidence record queryable by `path_id`, `commit_sha`, and `build_id` — automated compliance reporting (PTN-GOV-AI-004) becomes viable and manual evidence assembly is eliminated
- EA Practice reviews the specification once at the catalog level; every path whose template conforms inherits that review without individual template re-evaluation

**Implementation Complexity:** Medium

**Prerequisites:** Verification Contract Layer 1 and Layer 2 check IDs finalized (GUID-GOV-IMPL-001 Phases 1–3); scaffold template authored with confirmed unit test invocation pattern; approved container registry endpoint and OIDC workload identity configured for CI/CD runners

**Related Patterns:** PTN-INFRA-GOV-001, PTN-APP-GOV-001, PTN-INFRA-GOV-002, PTN-APP-GOV-003, PTN-GOV-AI-003, PTN-GOV-AI-001, PTN-GOV-AI-004
